title: Kamoʻoalewa, Earth's quasi-moon
hook: A small asteroid loops around Earth and may be a chip off the Moon.
peek: Kamoʻoalewa is a small asteroid that orbits the Sun in step with Earth, so from here it seems to circle us. Its colour looks like Moon rock, and many scientists now think it is a piece of the Moon.
lede: In 2016 the Pan-STARRS telescope on Haleakalā, Hawaii, found a small asteroid, probably somewhere between 40 and 100 metres across. It orbits the Sun, not Earth, but its orbit is so close to ours that it seems to loop around us year after year. Astronomers call this a quasi-satellite. Its Hawaiian name refers to a moving celestial fragment.

bullets.text: A quasi-satellite shares a planet's orbital period, drifting slightly inside and outside its path, so from Earth it seems to circle us. Kamoʻoalewa is expected to keep this dance going for centuries before it wanders off.

In 2021 astronomers found its reflected light matched weathered Moon rock better than typical asteroids. A later study suggested it could have been knocked loose by the impact that made the Giordano Bruno crater.
China's Tianwen-2 mission, launched in 2025, reached Kamoʻoalewa in mid-2026. It is due to collect a sample and bring it back to Earth in late 2027, which could settle where it came from.
